newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bond yields were little changed in late Monday trade after drifting sideways for most of what dealers desribed as a thin and directionless session.
At 1400 GMT, the bellwether R150 loan was pegged at a 14.31 pct yield from 14.315 percent late on Friday.
"It's been dead all day," a trader said. "There was a bit of offshore selling this morning which hiked the yields up and at the moment we are seeing a bit of buying into weakness."
Another trader said that local jobbers, eyeing a break above technical resistance around the 14.31/32 percent, were seen selling late in the afternoon session.
Dealers said the dearth of activity on the day stemmed from the fact that the market had no new news to feed on.

The market has focussed its attention on the rand in recent weaks as it came under pressure from speculators looking to nudge the currency over the 4.56 level, only to be stopped by Reserve Bank intervention on Friday, dealers said.
The rand was trading at 4.5535/5565 against the U.S. unit late on Monday -- unmoved from its late Friday level.
Dealers said the only activity seen on the day had been local importer demand which first surfaced in the morning session and again towards the local close.
"There was a bit of foreign interest but nothing worth commenting on," a trader said.
In the short-term the rand was expected to trade between 4.5450 and 4.57 in the absence of any significant developments.
"I don't see much on the horizon that can drive it for the time being," the trader added.
The rand's performance against the dollar was upstaged by its gains against the mark, which plumbed six-year lows against the U.S. currency in Europe.
The rand was last quoted at 0.3932/3936 marks from 0.3882/3886 marks on Friday after earlier touching 0.3944 bid -- the rand's strongest level against the mark since February last year.
Elsewhere, the rand was trading at 7.6900/6973 against sterling from 7.7076/7182 previously and at 25.0213/0445 yen from 24.9835/0110 on Friday.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 7.360 billion rand on Saturday from 7.355 billion rand on Saturday.
Foreigners were net buyers of 285.38 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling 746.16 million rand's worth on Thursday, the Bond Exchange said.
Exchange turnover totalled 5.9 billion rand on Friday from 43.7 billion rand on Thursday, a settlement date.
